under_vocal_policy.meaning: Under the vocal (bars 0, 2, 6 and beats 2-3 of bar 5) the band plays chords, bass and drums only. No clarinet / glockenspiel tune (the ezgi_alti stem is not used in 'dogal'), no pad, no counter-line. The Old MacDonald tune is heard only in the intro, the loud answers (bars 1 and 7) and the ending.

why_no_tune.text: shares of the sung time: the soft tune would sound a different note than the voice 86.7 % of the time and a second or seventh away from it 21.0 % of the time (two melodies at once, what the user rejected). It also does not fit the chords that support the voice: only 42.9 % of the tune's own time is on chord tones of the chosen harmony and 21.4 % clashes (its 'do do do' lies a semitone above the third of the dominant in bars 2 and 6).

why_no_pad.text: With chords, bass and drums only, a band note one semitone from the voice sounds for 4.5 % of the sung time (1.1 % in runs over 150 ms). A sustained pad cannot lower that (root + fifth 4.7 %, full triads 4.9 %) and a pad that holds the dominant seventh would triple it (15.2 %). The oom-pah already states every chord on each off-beat and on beats 1 and 3, so a pad adds nothing the voice needs.

under_vocal_policy.allowed_fallback_if_the_mix_step_finds_t: a very soft sustained pad of root + fifth or of the plain triads of the plan (never the seventh of the dominant, never a moving line). Its level is not decided here.

F major reaches the same chord tones only when no rule applies (the search then picks the very same triads); as soon as the loud answer has to be reached from I, IV or V and bar 6 has to end on V7 or I, the last note of lines 2 and 4 (D) is in neither chord: the phrase ends are chord tones for 52.8 % of their time in F against 100.0 % in C, and sustained clashes rise to 6.2 %. C is first inside the rules for the weights 1, 2 and 4. In C the triad that fits lines 2 and 4 (G B D) is the DOMINANT, so every sung phrase that ends on it is answered by the tonic.

how_the_plan_was_chosen.step_1: Every sequence of I ii iii IV V V7 vi (one chord per beat) was measured for each sung bar in C, F and G: 3 x (3 x 2401 + 49) = 21756 sequences (adaylar.json). Ranking J = chord_tone - 2 * (clash_sustained + outside_scale), the score designer A uses.
how_the_plan_was_chosen.step_2: Progression rules (kod/kurallar.py): bar 6 ends on V, V7 or I; the chord before a bar that is not sung is I, IV, V or V7; the dominant only goes to the tonic; at least two beats of I, IV, V per sung bar. Ties within 0.005: fewer chord changes, two-beat chords, more on-beat chord tones. Result in C: ii ii I I | V V V V7 | I I | V V V V7. A second rule set that also allows the turnaround V - IV - I gives V IV I I in bar 0 (the runner-up).
how_the_plan_was_chosen.step_3: The seventh of the dominant, decided by what really sounds (band model checked against the builder's MIDI, and rendered audio): the symbolic optimum puts V7 on the last beat of bars 2 and 6 because a sung F then counts as a chord tone; in the band that F sounds while the singer's E is next to it. Without the seventh nothing sounds a semitone from the voice in bars 2 and 6.

robustness.note: For each reading the best sequence inside the rule set is searched again (J on the frames of that bar's line, ties as in 03_tara.py). 'same harmony as chosen': strict rules: bar 0 = ii ii I I; turnaround rules: bar 0 = V IV I I; both: bar 5 = I I, bars 2 and 6 = the dominant on all four beats (V or V7 on each beat; whether the band plays the seventh is stage 2). J_deficit = J of the reading's pick minus J of the chosen sequence in the same reading (0 = the chosen sequence is the pick). For bars 2 and 6 the deficit of the chosen V V V V is mostly the stage-2 question (a sung F counts as a chord tone only when the symbol is V7); J_deficit_of_the_best_dominant_only_sequence shows what the HARMONY 'dominant on all four beats' loses against the reading's pick (0 in 16 of 18 readings).
robustness.weights: bar 0 = ii ii I I for the weights 1, 2 and 4 (strict rules) and V IV I I for all three (turnaround rules); bars 2 and 6 stay on the dominant for all three; with weight 4 bar 5 flips to V V (see trade-offs).

how_the_plan_was_chosen.cross_checks: The frame table reproduces the pitch-class histogram of kesim.json and matches an independent pitch track of the PLACED vocal (vokal_dogal.wav). The metric code is an independent re-implementation of designer A's and gives the same numbers for the baselines, the original loop and A's plan. kod/07_dogrula.py recomputes the numbers of this file by two separate routes.

reasoning: The sung melody is not the Old MacDonald tune. Its notes are D E F G A, G alone is 45.2 % of the sung time. Under the plain harmony I I IV I only 58.0 % of the sung time is on chord tones, 7.6 % is in sustained clashes (14 runs) and the last note of a line is a chord tone only 47.3 % of its time.

Line 1 (D on beat 0, G on the half beat, A A A on beat 1 | G G | G F E). The two strong notes of the first half are D and A; D minor is the only diatonic triad of C major that holds both, so ii carries beats 0-1 as ONE two-beat chord: on-beat chord tones of the line 97.5 % against 61.9 % for I IV and 17.3 % for the plain harmony. The G on the half beat is short (108 ms on G, the voice is on A from beat 0.78). Beats 2-3 rest on I: G and the final E are chord tones, the F in between passes. These are the very chords this vocal was made over in the original take (Dm Dm C C), now heard as ii - I of C major.

Lines 2 and 4 (D G | G G | F E | F E D). The first half is G: I, iii and V all hold it. In the second half F (on the beat) and E (off the beat) alternate: every triad with an F rubs the E and every triad with an E rubs the F; G B D is the only diatonic triad with neither, and it holds the final D. So V for the whole bar: no clash at all in line 2 (0.0 %), 1.4 % in line 4 (the mis-pitched first syllable of verses 3 and 7), against 8.4 % and 14.3 % sustained under the plain harmony. The phrase closes on the fifth of the dominant and the band answers on the tonic.

'diye bagirir' (G G | G F E) stays on I, as in the original take: 81.9 % chord tones, the final E is the third of the tonic. On rendered audio V V does not lower the rub there and supports the voice less (69.8 % against 79.5 % of the time).

No minor chord other than ii helps, and no chord of F or G major does better inside the rules: with all seven chords free on every beat the search returns the tonic and the dominant for bars 2, 5 and 6, exactly what designer A found with three chords. The freedom of this design changes one thing, the first half of bar 0.

Result against the plain harmony: chord tones 58.0 -> 69.2 %, sustained clash 7.6 -> 1.1 % (14 -> 3 runs in the whole song), on-beat chord tones 61.4 -> 68.9 %, phrase ends on a chord tone 47.3 -> 100.0 %, a band note a semitone from the voice 14.4 -> 4.5 % of the sung time. Against the ORIGINAL D minor loop the plan has about the same chord tones (69.2 against 72.7 %) and a fraction of its sustained clashes (1.1 against 15.8 %).

Sense of key: 30 of the 32 beats of a verse are on I or V(7); the only other chord is ii for two beats, and it resolves to the tonic inside its own bar, so each loud answer is entered from I (bar 0) or from V (bar 6).
trade_offs_stated_plainly: The chosen plan is not the highest-scoring one. The runner-up (V IV I I in bar 0) has 3.3 points more chord tones in note mode (0.6 in frame mode) and fewer major seconds between band and voice in beats 0-1; it was placed second for the harmonic rhythm and the progression, not for its fit.
Every verse opens on a minor chord for two beats. Whether that colour suits the cheerful band was not heard by anyone.

On the half beat of beat 0 the sung G sits between the F and the A of the D minor strum (two major seconds, about 108 ms per verse). The runner-up and designer A's bar double that G instead; designer A's bar leaves the D on the downbeat a major second above the piano's C.

In bars 2 and 6 the band plays no seventh, so the F and E of the animal word and of 'Ali Baba'nin' float above the G triad as seventh and sixth: chord tones 62.6 / 59.8 % there, below the plain harmony's 64.9 / 65.2 %, and a band note a whole tone from the voice sounds for about a third of those lines. That is the price of having no semitone rub at all in them.
What remains: the passing F of '-ligi var' and 'bagirir' over the C chord (4.5 % of the sung time a semitone from a sounding band note; 3 runs just over 150 ms in the whole song).

Bar 5 is the least certain bar: I I wins in note mode (J 0.7193 against 0.6266) and V V in frame mode, where the glide G - F sharp - F counts as one long clash against C. I I was kept because the line ends on E, the third of the tonic, and because the rendered audio shows no gain for V V.

The chord-level metrics treat every chord as sounding for its whole beat; the band model and the rendered audio correct for that, but the ii voicing they use is a proposal, not something the builder has rendered in the full mix.
not_verified_by_ear: Nobody listened. Verified by code: the frame table reproduces kesim.json and matches the placed vocal, the band model reproduces the builder's MIDI for I, IV and V7, the tune model reproduces the stem's MIDI, the metric code reproduces designer A's numbers, and 07_dogrula.py recomputes this file by separate routes. Unverified by ear: that ii at the verse opening sounds right in the cheerful band, that the dominant without its seventh is full enough, that the remaining passing F is harmless, and the ranking of the chosen plan against the runner-up.
